name: VA-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Walkinshaw with $2.8M raised vs. $11K for Purves
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 97%
model.rationale: The D+18 district, incumbent advantage, and overwhelming financial edge (about $2.8M raised versus $11K) all point to a comfortable Democratic win, and markets price the race near certain for Walkinshaw. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays at Safe D.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a dramatically tighter race or unexpected outside Republican spending would be the first sign of movement, though nothing currently suggests it.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Virginia's 11th District leans heavily Democratic, and first-term incumbent James Walkinshaw is running for a full term after winning the seat. He has raised about $2.8 million and holds nearly $1 million on hand, with substantial outside support, while Republican Arthur Purves has raised roughly $11,000 with almost no cash remaining. A Green Party candidate is also on the ballot but has shown no measurable activity.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on the district's strong partisan lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and prediction markets that price a Democratic win at about 97%. Everything points to Walkinshaw retaining the seat comfortably.
